We can't report this as happening on 12 June, and please don't give that date to anyone. A claim has to state what actually happened. If the date is wrong, an insurer can refuse the claim, cancel the policy or treat it as fraud.

What our records show:
- You found the water at about 21:00 on 11 June ("last night" in your email). You called us at 22:20 UK time that evening.
- Your Harbour Fen policy HF-CH-003 starts at 00:01 on 12 June.
- You don't know when the pipe first failed, but it must have been before you found the water.

That means the water was found before this policy started. On those facts, Harbour Fen is unlikely to cover it, but the decision is theirs. We only have the schedule, not the full policy wording.

Please tell us:
1. Did you have any home insurance in force on 11 June? For example, an earlier policy that this one replaced (with Harbour Fen or another insurer), or a buildings or block policy. If so, the claim belongs with that policy and should be reported promptly. Send us the insurer's name and policy number and we'll help. We're also checking whether we arranged any earlier cover for you.
2. Do you still want us to report this to Harbour Fen with the true facts? You're entitled to their decision, but it will probably be refused. A reported incident may stay on your claims record, and you may need to tell future insurers about it. Also, damage from this leak can't be claimed later under HF-CH-003 as if it were new.

Meanwhile:
- Keep the water off at the stopcock until a plumber has repaired the pipe. Ask them for a written note on the cause and how long the pipe was probably leaking. Keep the invoice.
- If water reached sockets, light fittings or the fuse box, don't touch them. Only switch off at the fuse box if it is dry and you aren't standing in water. Have an electrician check everything before you use it. Keep out of the room if the ceiling is sagging.
- Take photos before you dry anything out. Keep damaged items and the failed pipe until an insurer says they're not needed.

- Cover starts 12 June 2026 at 00:01 UK time, and the schedule was issued to the service desk on 10 June (`schedule.pdf`; `history.md` event 001).

1. **Make the timeline airtight.** The call note itself is stamped 21:20 UTC on 11 June, which is 22:20 UK summer time. Cover started at 00:01 UK time, which is 23:01 UTC on 11 June. So the discovery and the call both came before cover began, however "21:00" is read. Quote her own "last night" too.

She found the water at about 21:00 on 11 June and called us at 22:20 UK time that evening. The policy starts at 00:01 UK time on 12 June, so the water was found before cover began. The case stays open until she and our records team reply.
